# Pi adapter for the pinned pstack source

The behavior source is the `vendor/upstream/0.15.36/pstack/` snapshot at `c742dd61706fbacc1b95f1a20b7b988cf096ce6c`. Generated supported Skill/playbook entrypoints retain the upstream Markdown after this Pi prelude. The eleven core workflows have critical-rule mappings; preserving a source body does not prove that a model followed it. The full source inventory is pinned separately; maintainer semantic sign-off remains pending.

Apply user instructions and repository authority first. Read referenced source Markdown through `pstack_skill` with `upstream/skills/<skill>/...` resource IDs, consuming every page. Statechart's 0.15.36 TypeScript runtime and its test corpus are bundled under `skills/statechart/scripts`; the older 0.15.32 `.mjs` tools are retained for compatibility. Java/TLC and optional renderers are external dependencies. Other Cursor plugins, private APIs, drivers and cloud resources are not supplied.

For Statechart execution, run `node <skill-dir>/../../dist/statechart/statechart.js SPEC.tla [--config FILE] [--view FILE] [--out DIR]`. This compiled copy is required in installed packages because Node does not strip TypeScript inside `node_modules`. The upstream source and test corpus remain unchanged.

## Platform substitutions

- Task workers use `pstack_agents` and `pstack_workflow` Pi AgentSessions. The parent owns the playbook. Parallel writers use Git worktrees; integrated delivery uses an explicit integrator and verification. These are local processes, not cloud VMs or OS sandboxes.
- `/setup-pstack` previews model roles and suggested panels using models visible in the current Pi session; edit only what needs changing. Existing choices are preserved. Panels with the same model in several seats do not provide model diversity. Model roles use `models.json`; pass the playbook and, for named roles such as Reflect's `tooling`, `judgment`, `divergent`, and `synthesizer`, `modelRole` when dispatching. Explicit node models take precedence.
- Pi `thinkingLevel` replaces Cursor's reasoning slug conventions. Optional same-family fallback chooses a registered model from the same provider and reports it; a supported lower reasoning level may be used and reported. Unknown families are not guessed, Cursor `-fast` aliases are not rewritten, and authentication/inference failures are not automatically retried.
- For an unconfigured panel, plans suggest available Pi models and disclose repeated seats. Unresolvable configured seats are dropped or replaced with an available survivor or the parent, with notes. A known-family parent gets a judge only from another recognized family; if none is available, the plan produces candidates only and the coordinator must inspect, choose, integrate and verify them. A failed or unaccepted candidate is excluded only after the other candidates settle; verified survivors remain eligible and the dropout is recorded.
- Arena's cross-judge uses confined `pstack_candidates` access to verified worktrees. The integrator independently reads and compares candidates before selecting and grafting. Architect's template includes a separate implementation phase after the selected sketch; the coordinator still owns upstream grounding (`how`/`why`) and optional checkpoints.
- Interrogate creates a worktree for each adversary, copies the reviewed staged, unstaged and untracked changes, and runs a separate repro-verifier on each worktree. No adversary changes are integrated. Both sessions must report command, observed and expected output; synthesis can only carry reproductions present in a verifier report. These sessions use Pi's ordinary writable-agent shell permissions; the verification-policy allowlist controls native gate commands, not their interactive shell. Model reports are not independently attested receipts: the coordinator must inspect actual command evidence and the effect of any repro edits before claiming a finding is verified.
- Swarm supports partition, best-of, first-pass and rank-all race templates. First-pass waits for a candidate's deterministic acceptance, requests cooperative cancellation of the remaining sessions, and waits for them to settle. Rank-all reports every rank without automatically integrating a winner. Mixed partition/race still needs an explicit DAG.
- Custom Mode maps to sticky `/poteto-mode`. `/loop` maps to `/pstack-loop`, which requires an active Pi host and cannot promise cloud-root scheduling or exact delivery across a crash.
- Use an available named CLI/UI driver for real-surface proof. Without one, return blocked or inconclusive with the exact reason; unit tests, fake providers and worker reports cannot replace a live lane.

## Explicit policy deviations

- Native exact-head/base ledgers invalidate verification when either changes, including patch-preserving restacks; upstream can reuse some patch-ID-stable verdicts.
- Read-only reviewer, scout and verifier sessions inspect confined source and evidence but cannot run shell commands or live MCP. Deterministic commands run in an authorized runner or writable lane. For external investigation, the parent supplies evidence snapshots and verifies decisive citations.
- Autopilot templates prepare local DAG artifacts. The coordinator remains responsible for the owner lifecycle, early PRs, periodic audit, rebase discipline, countersigns and stop propagation. A stack template alone does not deliver a remote PR stack. Babysit stops at merge-ready; shipping and remote writes require the actual applicable authorization.
- Opening a PR does not start a babysit. Finish the phase or stack before a requested babysit unless an explicitly assigned full-autonomy owner owns the loop and has reported code-ready. Babysit stops before merge; operator-reserved items never merge automatically.

## Unsupported operations

`Cursor-private-PR-provenance`, `Cursor-watch-READY`, `Cursor-cleanup-plugin` and `Bugbot-pass-dismissal` are unsupported. GitHub/Origin and native states are alternatives with their own evidence boundaries, not proof that a Cursor operation ran. `make-bot-ui` and the Cursor automation event pack require Cursor-specific surfaces. Report these limitations rather than marking unavailable operations complete.

## Evidence boundary

`SEMANTICS.json` records selected critical-rule mappings, exact source lines, deviations, bound tests and file fingerprints. Inventory counts, source hashes, deterministic checks, Pi SDK/fake-provider tests, real-model runs and maintainer semantic review are separate evidence levels. Advancing the source pin and passing CI do not establish complete Cursor/Pi equivalence or maintainer approval.

## Pinned upstream instructions

Source: cursor/plugins@c742dd61706fbacc1b95f1a20b7b988cf096ce6c, pstack/skills/recall/SKILL.md. The following body is retained verbatim.


# Recall

**Before you start or resume work, you rebuild the user's recent working context and hand back a tight capsule of where things stand now and what to do next.**

Keep it tight and on-topic. Read only what the in-scope threads need, then stop.

Your context lives in two records. Your own chat history holds what you did and decided. The shared record holds everything that happened around the same code under other names: the symptoms users keep reporting, the fixes that shipped and got reverted, the errors still firing in prod. That second record is what the **why** skill searches, across source control, the issue tracker, chat and issue channels, long-form docs, and error tracking. A feature with a long bug tail keeps most of its story there, so don't reconstruct it from your transcripts alone.

Transcripts live at `~/.cursor/projects/<slug>/agent-transcripts/<uuid>/<uuid>.jsonl`, where `<slug>` is the workspace path with the leading slash dropped and each "/" turned into "-" (so `/Users/you/proj` becomes `Users-you-proj`). Every line is one chat message.

1. Classify, then route. One specific prior chat to resume is the `session-pickup` playbook, not this. Turning habits into a durable skill is `automate-me`. A human-readable summary of your work is a different task. Recall loads working context across recent chats before you act. If the user already gave you a full state capsule (paths, branch, the change), use it and skip the mining.
2. Lock the scope before searching. Pin the window ("recent" is a real range, default the last 7 days), the topic if named, and the workspace (default the active one. Never read another project's transcripts without being asked). State the scope back. Never quietly turn "all" into "recent N".
3. Fan out across your chat history. Spawn parallel subagents on a fast, cheap model, each taking a slice of the corpus. Tell every subagent to order candidates by real modification time (`ls -t`) and never by UUID name, grep the topic first and then read only the matching chats and only their relevant regions, and skip the current chat plus obvious noise (subagent, eval, and test chats). Each returns the same schema, one block per chat: topic, the user's goal, decisions, open threads, struggles and corrections, and artifacts (PRs, tickets, branches), each citing the chat UUID. For one or two chats, skip the fan-out and search directly. The raw transcripts stay in the subagents. The main thread gets only their findings. Pick each subagent's reasoning level and fast or standard speed for the job, per the Subagents section of the **poteto-mode** skill.
4. Sweep the shared record whenever the topic names a feature, file, subsystem, area, or bug. This is the default, not a judgment call, and "my work on X" does not exempt it. Hand it to the **why** skill's source investigators, but steer their question from "why was this built this way" to "what's the current state, what's been tried and didn't hold, and what are users still reporting". Reuse its per-source playbooks, run the investigators in parallel with the chat-history mining, and inherit its posture: one investigator per source, null results are findings, skip an unavailable MCP and say so. Fold what comes back into the brief. Skip this step only for pure activity recall with no named target ("what did I do this week"), where your own history and live state are the entire answer.
5. Verify against live state. Take the PRs, branches, and tickets that the mining and the sweep surfaced and check them with `git` and `gh`. When the answer hinges on what an agent actually did (the tools it ran, files it read, errors it hit), read the full transcript, not just a trimmed local copy.
6. Write the brief to the contract below. Group by thread. Stay on the named topic.

## Output contract

Lead with the capsule, then the thread status, then the problems, then the next move. Deeper detail goes below or gets cut.

- **Capsule.** At most 5 bullets. What this work is and where it stands overall.
- **Threads.** One line each, prefixed with exactly one status tag: `[merged #N]`, `[open PR #N]`, `[in flight <branch>]`, `[verified, uncommitted]`, `[reverted #N]`, or `[planned, not started]`. A thread with no tag is not done yet, so tag it.
- **Problems.** At most 5, the recurring ones. Include the symptoms users keep reporting and any fix that shipped and was reverted, so the next attempt starts where the last one failed.
- **Next move.** The single most useful next action, concrete.

An adjacent feature or ticket stays out unless it blocks this one. When the capsule and thread lines outgrow a screen, cut detail before you cut threads. Write the brief through the **unslop** skill, cite chat findings by UUID and shared-record findings by their source (PR #, ticket ID, chat permalink, error-tracker issue), and sanitize private context before any public output.

**Reply:** the brief, to the contract above.


## Pi execution tools

Use `pstack_agents` for one child and `pstack_workflow` / `pstack_graph` for an explicit DAG. Roles are `architect`, `worker`, `reviewer`, `verifier`, `synthesizer` and `integrator`. Parallel writers use isolated worktrees, then an integrator. A verifier directly depends on the artifact owner. Inspect workflow status on recovery; completed nodes are not replayed. Check remote state before retrying external effects. `pstack_worktrees` cleans only owned clean worktrees.
